target.title: fix(doctor): exit non-zero on final invalid config (#77804)
target.body:
## Summary

`openclaw doctor` printed `Invalid config:` validation errors but still exited `0`. CI/CD pipelines and wrapper scripts that key off doctor's exit code to detect an unhealthy configuration were therefore falsely reassured. This PR sets `process.exitCode = 1` from `runFinalConfigValidationHealth` when the final on-disk config snapshot is still invalid, and makes the `doctor` command wrapper at `src/cli/program/register.maintenance.ts` honor `process.exitCode` instead of unconditionally exiting `0`.

Fixes #77804.

The change is small and localized:

- `src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.ts` (+3): set `process.exitCode = 1` only if not already non-zero.
- `src/cli/program/register.maintenance.ts` (+1/-1): pass `process.exitCode` through to `defaultRuntime.exit(...)`.
- `src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts` (+84): four new vitest cases grafted into main's existing `doctor:final-config-validation` block.
- `src/cli/program/register.maintenance.test.ts` (+19): regression for the command-wrapper exit-code passthrough.

Rebased onto current `main` (was ~12k commits behind). Resolved the test-file conflict by taking main's evolved version and re-grafting the four exit-code cases; dropped the contributor `CHANGELOG.md` entry per repo policy.

## Still-needed validation (against current main)

Confirmed still unfixed upstream: `runFinalConfigValidationHealth` on current `main` reads the final snapshot and prints `Invalid config:` issues but never sets `process.exitCode`, and the `doctor` wrapper still calls `defaultRuntime.exit(0)` unconditionally.

## Real behavior proof

Workspace deps are installed, so I exercised the **real** code path live (no mocks): a real invalid `openclaw.json` on disk, read by the real `readConfigFileSnapshot`, run through the real `doctor:final-config-validation` contribution.

Behavior addressed: `openclaw doctor` returned exit code 0 even after printing `Invalid config:` errors from final validation.
Real environment tested: macOS, node 22.22.2, openclaw source at the rebased-onto-main HEAD. Ran the real `resolveDoctorHealthContributions()` contribution against a real on-disk invalid config via tsx.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: wrote an invalid `openclaw.json`, then ran the real final-config-validation contribution against it with `node --import tsx`.
Evidence after fix: live terminal output below.

```
$ cat $OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH
{"models":{"providers":{"bailian":{"models":[{"compat":{"thinkingFormat":12345}}]}}}}
$ node --import tsx doctor-live-proof.mts
INVALID config -> process.exitCode = 1
first reported errors: ["Invalid config:",
  "- models.providers.bailian.models.0.id: Invalid input: expected string, received undefined",
  "- models.providers.bailian.models.0.name: Invalid input: expected string, received undefined"]
```

Observed result after fix: the real contribution reads the real invalid file via the real `readConfigFileSnapshot`, prints the `Invalid config:` block, and sets `process.exitCode = 1`. With a valid or missing config it leaves `process.exitCode` at 0, and a non-zero code set earlier in the run is never lowered.
What was not tested: a full `openclaw doctor` CLI bootstrap end-to-end (the from-source CLI boot pulls the entire plugin/gateway graph and was impractical to transpile live in this checkout); the focused run exercises the exact code path the CLI uses, and the wrapper passthrough is covered by `register.maintenance.test.ts`.

## Automated tests

Both touched test files pass with deps reconciled:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts src/cli/program/register.maintenance.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  40 passed (40)
```

## Risks

Low. Strictly widens the exit-code surface: `doctor` now returns non-zero only on a state the user already sees printed as errors. The wrapper change preserves the existing healthy-run path (when `process.exitCode` is undefined or 0).

No `CHANGELOG.md` entry, per repo policy (release-owned).

target.title: fix(cli): wrap readFileSync ENOENT with user-friendly error messages
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three CLI code paths in `src/cli/` leak raw Node.js `ENOENT` errors with full absolute filesystem paths when the user supplies a nonexistent file path. This is noisy and exposes internal implementation details.

**Before (all three paths):**
```
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/home/user/.openclaw/some/internal/path'
```

**After:**
```
Error: --batch-file not found: /nonexistent/path/batch.json5
Error: Secrets plan file not found: /tmp/missing-plan.json
Error: --file not found: /bad/patch.json5
```

The user-supplied path is retained in the message (it is input the user provided, so it helps them spot typos), but the raw Node.js error code and any derived internal paths are removed. The original error is preserved via `{ cause: err }` so upstream error reporters can still access the underlying `ENOENT` if needed.

Fixes #N/A (no linked issue)

## Why This Change Was Made

Affected surfaces:

| File | User action | Error |
|------|-------------|-------|
| `src/cli/config-set-input.ts:139` | `openclaw config set --batch-file <bad-path>` | `ENOENT` raw error |
| `src/cli/secrets-cli.ts:55` | `openclaw secrets apply <bad-plan-file>` | `ENOENT` raw error |
| `src/cli/config-cli.ts:1497` | `openclaw config patch --file <bad-path>` | `ENOENT` raw error |

Each fix wraps `readFileSync` in a try-catch that checks `(err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT"` and throws a descriptive `Error` with the user-facing flag name, the original path, and the original error as `cause`. Non-ENOENT errors are re-thrown unchanged. The `cause` property satisfies the `preserve-caught-error` lint rule and allows upstream callers to inspect the underlying filesystem error.

## User Impact

- Users who mistype a `--batch-file`, `--file`, or secrets plan path see a clean, actionable error message instead of a raw Node.js stack trace.
- No change to the success path or any other error path. Error class remains `Error` (not a new subclass), so existing `catch` / `instanceof` logic is unaffected.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/cli/config-set-input.test.ts src/cli/secrets-cli.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts` — 156/156 passing (includes 3 ENOENT regression tests covering all 3 command paths)
- `oxlint --quiet` on all 6 touched files — clean
- `oxfmt --check` on all 6 touched files — clean

### Real CLI proof (after `pnpm build`)

**Command 1: `config set --batch-file`**
```
$ pnpm openclaw config set --batch-file /nonexistent/path/batch.json5
Error: --batch-file not found: /nonexistent/path/batch.json5
EXIT: 1
```

**Command 2: `config patch --file`**
```
$ pnpm openclaw config patch --file /nonexistent/path/patch.json5
Error: --file not found: /nonexistent/path/patch.json5
EXIT: 1
```

**Command 3: `secrets apply --from`**
```
$ pnpm openclaw secrets apply --from /nonexistent/path/plan.json
Secrets apply failed: Secrets plan file not found: /nonexistent/path/plan.json ...
EXIT: 1
```

Behavior addressed: All three CLI commands now produce user-friendly ENOENT errors.
Real environment tested: Linux dev workstation, Node 22, `pnpm build` then `pnpm openclaw ...`.
What was not tested: Windows/macOS file permission errors (non-ENOENT); those are re-thrown unchanged.

target.title: fix(ai): safely serialize non-Error stream failures to avoid circular crashes
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: the OpenAI Completions, Google, and Anthropic provider stream error handlers formatted a non-Error exception with a bare `JSON.stringify(error)`. `JSON.stringify` throws a `TypeError` on values containing circular references (network errors commonly carry circular socket refs) and on BigInt, so the error handler itself throws a second exception mid-failure, crashing the handler and preventing the stream from closing — unhandled rejections, fd leaks, and hung downstream stream consumers (issue #106570, and the identical Google case #106568).

**Solution**: add a shared `safeJsonStringify` helper (`try JSON.stringify` → fall back to `String(value)`) and use it in all three stream error handlers, so a non-serializable error degrades to a readable string instead of crashing. Mistral already had a private copy of this helper; it now consumes the shared one.

**What changed**: new `packages/ai/src/utils/safe-json-stringify.ts` (+ test); `JSON.stringify(error)` -> `safeJsonStringify(error)` in `openai-completions.ts`, `google-shared.ts`, `anthropic.ts`; `mistral.ts` imports the shared helper and drops its local duplicate.

**What did NOT change**: the `error instanceof Error ? error.message : ...` branch, all normal serialization output (plain objects/arrays/primitives serialize identically), the providers' success/abort paths, and any public API/config/CLI surface.

Fixes #106570
Fixes #106568

---

## Root Cause

**Trigger condition**: a provider stream fails with a non-Error value (e.g. a Node network error) whose object graph contains a circular reference.

**Root cause analysis**: `JSON.stringify` is a throwing operation used on the error-handling path, which must never throw again. On circular or BigInt values it throws `TypeError: Converting circular structure to JSON`, so the `catch` block that was supposed to record `errorMessage` crashes instead, leaving the stream un-closed. Root: unguarded serialization of untrusted error values.

**Affected scope**: the OpenAI Completions (#106570), Google (#106568), and Anthropic stream error handlers — the same one-line pattern in three providers. Anthropic had no filed issue but the identical bug and crash-loop, so it is fixed for consistency (preventive). `azure-openai-responses.ts` and `openai-responses.ts` already wrap `JSON.stringify` in try/catch and are not affected.

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: a non-Error stream failure with circular references no longer crashes the provider error handler; it degrades to a readable string and the stream closes.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.13.1, vitest v4.1.9. The crash is reproduced and fixed at source with a real Node run and a committed unit test.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: reproduce the raw crash, then show the shared helper is safe on the same value.
```bash
# node repro of the exact crash on a non-Error error carrying a circular socket ref
node -e 'const socket={}; const err={code:"ECONNRESET",socket}; socket.parent=err; JSON.stringify(err)'
# node vitest run of the shared helper on the same kind of value (no throw)
node node_modules/.bin/vitest run packages/ai/src/utils/safe-json-stringify.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
Before fix (bare JSON.stringify on a circular non-Error error): the handler throws.
    TypeError: Converting circular structure to JSON
        --> starting at object with constructor 'Object'
        |     property 'socket' -> object with constructor 'Object'
        --- property 'parent' closes the circle

After fix (safeJsonStringify): no throw; degrades to a readable string.
    safeJsonStringify(err) === "[object Object]"
    Test Files  1 passed (1)
         Tests  6 passed (6)     # asserts JSON.stringify(circular) throws and safeJsonStringify does not
```

**Observed result after the fix**: the same circular non-Error value that made `JSON.stringify` throw is handled safely; the committed test asserts both the crash (`expect(() => JSON.stringify(circular)).toThrow(TypeError)`) and the safe result. Provider regressions pass (openai-completions + anthropic 111, mistral + helper 24).

**What was not tested**: driving a full live provider stream to failure with a real circular network error (substituted by the source-level repro above, which exercises the exact serialization path the handlers use).

## Tests and validation

### Unit tests
```
$ node node_modules/.bin/vitest run packages/ai/src/utils/safe-json-stringify.test.ts --no-coverage
 Tests  6 passed (6)      # circular, network-error-with-circular-socket, undefined/function, BigInt, plain objects, primitives

$ node node_modules/.bin/vitest run packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.test.ts packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.test.ts
 Tests  111 passed (111)  # provider regression
$ node node_modules/.bin/vitest run packages/ai/src/providers/mistral.test.ts packages/ai/src/utils/safe-json-stringify.test.ts
 Tests  24 passed (24)    # mistral consolidation regression

$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json ...     # no type errors in changed files
$ node node_modules/.bin/oxlint <6 changed files>          # exit 0
```

## Risk checklist

merge-risk: Low

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation (N/A - internal error-serialization helper, no public API/config/CLI/doc surface)
- [x] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary (none)

Mitigation: `safeJsonStringify` returns output identical to `JSON.stringify` for all normally-serializable values; it only diverges where `JSON.stringify` would throw (circular/BigInt) or return `undefined` (undefined/functions), turning a crash into a readable string. The mistral change is an equivalent swap to the shared helper.

## Current review state

- [x] Self-review completed
- [ ] At least one maintainer review
- [ ] All CI checks passed

---

> AI-assisted: root-cause analysis, implementation, and tests were prepared with AI assistance and human-reviewed.

target.title: feat(control-ui): upload files into terminals
target.body:
Closes #107289

**AI-assisted:** built with Codex. I reviewed the implementation and understand the upload, staging, cleanup, node relay, and terminal-input paths.

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI terminal had no way to move a local file to the machine that owns the PTY. Operators had to arrange a separate transfer before they could reference an image, PDF, archive, or other local file in a terminal command.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add drag-and-drop plus a multi-file paperclip picker. Each file is size-bounded, staged on the Gateway or paired node that owns the terminal, and returned as a shell-quoted absolute path at the cursor without pressing Enter.

Uploads remain admin-only and bound to an already-open terminal session. Files use private per-user staging, expire after 24 hours, and recover cleanup after process restarts. Windows uses the user-profile ACL boundary; POSIX hosts use directory mode `0700` and file mode `0600`.

Path insertion recognizes PowerShell, `cmd.exe`, and known POSIX shell dialects. Every unknown shell override fails closed instead of guessing quoting semantics; `cmd.exe` also refuses full paths containing `%` or `!` expansion syntax.

## User Impact

Operators can drop images, PDFs, archives, and other files directly into an active Control UI terminal, or select one or many files with the paperclip button. Each file may be up to 16 MiB. Older paired nodes keep terminal access but do not offer uploads until their pairing capability is upgraded. An unrecognized custom shell receives an explicit refusal rather than a possibly unsafe path; running OpenClaw inside WSL provides native Linux paths.

## Evidence

- Focused protocol, Gateway, node-host, infrastructure, and Control UI tests: 128 passed.
- Final canonical-base64 and unknown-shell hardening plus surrounding Gateway, staging, and Control UI tests: 30 passed.
- Control UI i18n: 14 tests passed; all 20 locales clean with zero English fallbacks.
- Chromium E2E: multi-select PDF/TXT upload, PNG drop, distinct base64 payloads, quoted path insertion, and no carriage return/newline: passed.
- Chromium baseline/current visual capture: `origin/main` has no upload affordance; this branch shows the paperclip action.
- Source-blind behavior contract: picker, drop, transfer payload, quoting, and no-execution expectations passed.
- Plugin SDK API baseline, Control UI fallback baseline, targeted lint, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Remote Blacksmith proof: Control UI Chromium passed on both branch and baseline; all touched changed-check lanes passed. A later unrelated moving-main wizard lint failure was fixed on `main` by `69e2282c46d25`.
- Autoreview: cleanup retry/recovery, Windows shell quoting, Git Bash quoting, Windows ACL staging, unknown-shell fail-closed behavior, UNC detection, `cmd.exe` full-path expansion, and canonical base64 findings addressed; final fix review clean.

### Before

Archived `origin/main` Chromium capture: no terminal upload button. Automated assertion: `button.tp-upload` count is `0`.

### After

Current-head Chromium capture: paperclip visible and enabled. Automated picker/drop workflow passes. Both captures were visually inspected locally.

## Documentation

Updated Control UI usage, Gateway protocol, paired-node terminal upload behavior, localization, and the supported Windows shell boundary.

## Release note

Control UI terminals now accept drag-and-drop or multi-select file uploads and paste safe paths on the terminal host.

target.title: fix(azure): responses model aliases route correctly
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users configuring `azure-openai-responses/*` could have model status probes and embedded-agent runs resolve through the OpenAI owner/auth path instead of the configured Azure Responses credentials and base URL.

The inverse boundary also matters: OpenAI-owned, manifest-suppressed models such as `gpt-5.3-codex-spark` must still produce the OpenAI OAuth remediation instead of being misclassified as an Azure deployment.

Closes #93781

## Why This Change Was Made

Alias canonicalization now considers the requested model together with configured Azure endpoint/model surface and manifest suppressions before choosing the provider owner. Configured Azure models and custom deployments keep `azure-openai-responses`; endpoint-less aliases and explicitly suppressed OpenAI models canonicalize to `openai`.

Configured overrides also carry the requested provider onto discovered model rows, so Azure API/base URL/auth ownership is preserved after catalog lookup. This does not change public config, schema, migrations, credential storage, or the OpenAI plugin manifest.

When an Azure provider config supplies its endpoint and credential but omits the optional `api` field, the resolver now consumes the transport API declared by the retained manifest alias before discovered OpenAI metadata. It does not infer an API from arbitrary provider ids, so params-only GitHub Copilot configurations keep their discovered per-model protocols.

## User Impact

Azure Responses users can probe and run configured `azure-openai-responses` models without OpenClaw silently switching to an OpenAI auth profile. Provider-level Azure deployment names remain Azure-owned, Codex-only models continue to point users to the correct OpenAI OAuth flow, and GitHub Copilot Enterprise params-only configs retain Anthropic/OpenAI transports selected per model.

## Evidence

- Rebuilt the stale branch on the pinned `main` snapshot `6eae468d4573d9f4193f266789cd5ea9d979f61b` and resolved the two overlapping static-catalog source/test conflicts. The merge-base is exactly that SHA, the effective submission contains no inherited branch changes, and the diff is limited to eight embedded-agent resolver/test files.
- Focused resolver regression suite:

  ```text
  Test Files  3 passed (3)
  Tests       194 passed (194)
  Duration    33.74s
  ```

  The suite includes discovered and configured-fallback Azure cases with `baseUrl` configured and `api` omitted; a retained manifest alias carrying both `api` and `baseUrl`; a retained alias with no provider config; and params-only GitHub Copilot Claude, Gemini, and GPT cases. target.title: fix(codex): keep omitted-final source replies from releasing the turn
target.body:
Closes #106961

## What Problem This Solves

In `message_tool_only` delivery mode, the Codex app-server treated any delivered `message` source reply as terminal unless the model explicitly passed `final: false`. An agent that sent an early progress update ("on it, will report back") had its turn released immediately: the remaining tool calls and the real final reply never ran. From the user's side the agent posts one status line and then goes silent (log signal: `codex app-server turn released after terminal dynamic tool result`).

## Why This Change Was Made

The projected `final` schema control tells the model to "set true **only when** this message is intended to complete the reply" - so models naturally omit `final` on progress sends, and the runtime contradicted its own schema by terminating anyway.

This change makes inferred source-reply delivery release the turn only on explicit `final: true`, matching the generic embedded-runner contract established in #92343: intermediate delivery continues the turn, and termination follows the normal Codex `turn/completed` lifecycle.

Safety properties preserved:

- The `sourceReplyFinal` completed marker for omitted `final` is unchanged, so stranded-reply recovery still cannot re-deliver a duplicate of a delivered reply.
- Duplicate end-block suppression via `didDeliverSourceReplyViaMessageTool` is unchanged.
- Tool-owned `terminate` results and yield results still release as before.
- Mixed dynamic-tool batch semantics (`resolveTerminalDynamicToolBatchAction`) are untouched.

The `final` schema description now also tells models that omitting it keeps the turn alive, so the control is learnable instead of discipline-based.

## User Impact

Codex-backed agents on Discord/Telegram/etc. can post intermediate progress messages and keep executing until the work is done. Explicit `final: true` still stops the turn after confirmed delivery.

## Evidence

- `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts`: 99/99 pass. Omitted-final delivered replies are now non-terminal with a completed marker; explicit `final: true` still releases across implicit sends, explicit source routes, receipt-confirmed replies, and middleware-redacted receipts.

target.title: fix(feishu): add chunk-idle timeout to inbound media download
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a stalled Feishu (Lark SDK) inbound media download body blocks the channel's agent-reply workflow indefinitely because the underlying Node.js `Readable` async iterator never settles on empty/stalled streams. Additionally preserves the established Feishu timeout policy: the per-chunk idle timeout is derived from the canonical `resolveConfiguredHttpTimeoutMs()` resolver (respecting `OPENCLAW_FEISHU_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS` env var, account config, and default) instead of a hardcoded 30s value.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Wrap each `AsyncIterable.next()` call in `Promise.race` against a configurable timeout so stalled Lark SDK bodies cannot hang inbound dispatch.
- **Do NOT `await` iterator.return()** in the finally block — Node Readable async-iterator `return()` hangs when the underlying source is stalled (waits for a `readable` event that never fires). Instead, explicitly **destroy** the source on timeout so the underlying Readable (and its HTTP resource) close, then call `iterator.return()` without awaiting.
- Thread the canonical Feishu timeout (`resolveConfiguredHttpTimeoutMs`) from `saveMessageResourceFeishu()` through `saveMessageResourceWithType()` → `saveFeishuResponseMedia()` → `saveMediaStreamWithIdleTimeout()`, so the per-chunk idle deadline respects the user's configured HTTP timeout policy.
- ClawSweeper Maintainer option 1 (**Cancel and prove the source**): implemented — timeout path calls `destroySource()`; focused + HTTP loopback proofs assert `destroyed=true` and server-side connection close.
- No new config/env surface. The timeout inherits the existing Feishu HTTP timeout policy.

Collision check: searched open PRs for "feishu chunk-idle timeout media download stall"; no same-file or same-problem open PR was found.

target.title: fix(gateway): force-discard ACP runtime after cancel/close timeout
target.body:
Closes #106631

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who send `/reset` after an ACP-backed session hits a stuck cancel/close (for example after a model/API error poisoned the session) would still get the same broken runtime on the next message. The gateway timed out ACP cancel/close, returned “try again in a moment,” and left the cached runtime handle in place, so recovery required restarting the whole gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

When ACP cancel or close hits the bounded cleanup timeout, the gateway now calls a manager-owned `forceDiscardSession` path that **detaches** the cached runtime handle immediately **outside** the session actor queue (a timed-out cancel may still own that queue) and best-effort closes the detached runtime without awaiting a second hang. Session-reset then continues into the existing fresh-reset / meta path so the next message cannot reuse the stale process. Normal successful cancel→close is unchanged.

Compatibility: additive manager method only; no config, protocol, or public CLI shape changes. Performance: force-discard runs only on the timeout recovery path. Usability: `/reset` can recover without a gateway restart. Security: only the session being reset/deleted is discarded; no auth or approval widening.

## User Impact

Operators and channel users whose ACP session gets stuck can recover with `/reset` even when cancel/close times out, instead of needing a full gateway restart that disrupts every session.

## Evidence

Focused local Vitest on macOS (Crabbox not used):

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/acp/control-plane/manager.runtime-handles.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server.sessions.reset-cleanup.test.ts

# results
✓ manager.runtime-handles.test.ts (14 tests) — force-discard eviction + hanging-close detach
✓ server.sessions.reset-cleanup.test.ts (22 tests) — cancel-timeout and close-timeout force-discard
```

Path-scoped formatting: `oxfmt` on the four touched files — pass.
`git diff --check` — pass.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: `/reset` (and session-delete cleanup) no longer leaves a reusable ACP runtime handle when cancel or close hits the bounded cleanup timeout. Force-discard **detaches the cache entry immediately**, then best-effort closes the detached runtime **without awaiting**, so a second hang on process close cannot stall reset/delete recovery.
- Environment: local macOS openclaw checkout; focused Vitest via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (Verification host: local macOS, Crabbox bypass).
- Current-main contrast: on current main, `closeAcpRuntimeForSession` returns `UNAVAILABLE` on cancel/close timeout without clearing the runtime handle cache, so the next message can reuse the same process.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/acp/control-plane/manager.runtime-handles.test.ts -t "force-discards"`
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions.reset-cleanup.test.ts -t "force-discards ACP"`
  3. Full sibling suites for both files as listed in Evidence (14 + 22 tests).
- Evidence after fix:
  - Manager (cancel still owns actor): `forceDiscardSession` detaches/closes with `reason: session-reset`; next turn re-ensures (`ensureSession` twice).
  - Manager (hanging runtime close): `forceDiscardSession` **resolves without waiting** on a never-resolving `runtime.close`; next turn still re-ensures a fresh session.
  - Gateway cancel-timeout: short cleanup timeout + hanging cancel → `sessions.reset` succeeds, `forceDiscardSession` once for `agent:main:main` / `session-reset`, no `closeSession`, fresh ACP meta restored.
  - Gateway close-timeout: cancel succeeds, hanging `closeSession` times out → `forceDiscardSession` once; reset still completes and restores pending ACP meta.
- Control check: normal happy-path `sessions.reset closes ACP runtime handles for ACP sessions` still expects `closeSession` and does not force-discard; only the timeout branches use force-discard.
- Observed result after fix: both cancel-timeout and close-timeout reset paths recover without leaving a reusable stale handle, and force-discard cannot re-block on a stuck process close.
- What was not tested: live Telegram/Feishu ACP channel recording with a real stuck backend process; full 15s production cleanup timeout wall-clock (tests use a short override for the race only).

## AI disclosure

This PR was authored with AI assistance (Grok).

target.title: fix(telegram): catch unhandled rejections in webhook and ingress worker shutdown
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram webhook shutdown could leave owned resources active when an early teardown step failed: a synchronous `server.close()` throw, a `bot.stop()` rejection, or a transport-close rejection could skip later cleanup (bot stop, undici transport close, webhook status, diagnostic heartbeat). Ingress-worker `stop()` could also race on repeated calls and leave `worker.terminate()` rejections unobserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Independently guard each ordered webhook shutdown phase via `runTelegramWebhookShutdownPhases` so one sync/async failure cannot skip later owned cleanup, and wrap the path so fire-and-forget abort listeners never leak unhandled rejections. Startup failure cleanup uses `.catch(() => undefined)` so cleanup noise cannot mask the original startup error. Ingress-worker `stop()` shares one in-flight promise and observes terminate rejections.

## User Impact

Operators restarting or aborting a Telegram webhook account no longer risk leaked transports, stale webhook connected status, or leftover diagnostic heartbeats when one shutdown step fails. Process logs no longer see unhandled rejections from webhook/ingress shutdown paths.

## Evidence

Exact head: `115b318a0602120489ca3f2597577e118a16c4ee`

### Focused tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts -- --run -t "does not leak unhandled|does not skip"
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/webhook-shutdown.proof.test.ts -- --run
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts -- --run
```

Observed: 4 webhook shutdown tests passed; proof test passed; 3 ingress-worker tests passed.

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: sync `server.close()` throw must not skip bot/transport/status/diagnostics cleanup.
Real environment tested: local Node production-path helper + negative nested-control-flow control (no live Telegram token required for this cleanup contract).

Exact commands run:

```bash
node --import tsx extensions/telegram/src/proof-telegram-webhook-shutdown.mts
```

Observed output after fix:

```text
node=v22.22.0
head=dc6452bf7ea4f208caf64f87c03019d1eeb86d2d

[case 1] negative control — sync server.close throw skips later cleanup
  ok: closeServer ran once
  ok: stopBot was skipped
  ok: closeTransport was skipped
  ok: noteStop was skipped
  ok: stopDiagnostics was skipped
  ok: outer catch logged unexpected error
  info: closeServer=1 stopBot=0 closeTransport=0 noteStop=0 stopDiagnostics=0 errors=1

[case 2] positive control — sync server.close throw continues cleanup
  ok: abort + drain + closeServer ran
  ok: stopBot still ran
  ok: closeTransport still ran
  ok: noteStop still ran
  ok: stopDiagnostics still ran
  ok: server close failure was logged
  ok: shutdown promise did not reject
  info: stopBot=1 closeTransport=1 noteStop=1 stopDiagnostics=1 errors=["webhook server close failed: server close failed"]

[case 3] valid path — clean server.close runs full teardown
  ok: every phase ran exactly once
  ok: no errors logged on clean path
  info: phases_ok=true errors=0

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 15 passed, 0 failed
```

Evidence:
- Negative control reproduces the pre-fix nested try/finally skip.
- Positive control proves guarded phases continue after sync close throw.
- Valid path proves clean close still runs full ordered teardown.
- Vitest integration: `server.close` monkeypatch on a real started webhook still runs stop/transport/status/diagnostics with no unhandledRejection.

What was not tested: live configured Telegram Bot API gateway restart with a real bot token (cleanup contract is local HTTP + owned transport teardown, not Bot API delivery).

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large base64-encoded images can cause transient memory pressure during decoding. This PR adds a size estimation check before decoding base64 image data in CLI staging and provider image-parsing paths, and propagates the existing configured media size limit through these new guards.

**Security impact**: Defense-in-depth against transient memory exhaustion from oversized base64 payloads.

## Summary

- Added `estimateBase64DecodedSize` helper that estimates decoded byte length from base64 input
- Propagated existing `maxBytes` limit through:
  - CLI image writing (`writeCliImages`)
  - Provider image parsing (`generatedImageAssetFromBase64`)
- Added boundary tests for:
  - Configured limit acceptance (7MB payload under 8MB limit)
  - Over-limit rejection before decoding
  - Default limit enforcement (6 MiB)
- **No new configuration**: Uses existing `generatedMediaMaxBytes` setting

## Evidence

**Environment**: macOS Vitest (Node 22.22.2)

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
# Run configured limit test
npx vitest run src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts
```

**Observed result after fix**:
```text
✓ agents-core src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts (30 tests) 203ms
✓ agents-support src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts (30 tests) 184ms

Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests  60 passed (60)

Key test coverage:
✓ rejects base64 image that exceeds size limit
✓ accepts images above MAX_IMAGE_BYTES when a higher configured maxBytes is provided
  - 7MB payload accepted under 8MB configured limit (line 322-346)
  - 10MB payload rejected under 8MB limit
  - 7MB payload rejected under default 6MiB limit (no maxBytes)
```

**Configuration limit propagation verified**:
- Test file: `src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts:322-346`
- Scenario: 7MB payload (above default 6MiB) accepted when 8MB limit configured
- Code path: `writeCliImages` receives `maxBytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024`, checks pass

**What was not tested**: Live provider OOM reproduction (neither necessary nor safely desirable)

## Regression Test Plan
- Coverage: 60 tests across 2 test suites
- Target files: `src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts`, `src/image-generation/image-assets.test.ts`
- Scenarios locked in:
  - Estimated size < maxBytes: accept
  - Estimated size > maxBytes: reject before decode
  - Configured limit > default: use configured
  - No configured limit: use default 6 MiB

target.title: fix(workspaces): reject non-decimal --grid segments via strict parser
target.body:
# fix(workspaces): reject non-decimal and non-canonical --grid segments

> Owner-boundary fix at the CLI `--grid` parser. Mirrors the merged pattern in
> #106384 (google-meet `--since`) and #106926 (onepassword `audit --limit`):
> swap a bare `Number()` coercion for the shared `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger`
> helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/number-runtime`, so JS-coercion forms
> (`0x10`, `1e2`, `0o10`, `0b10`, `-1`, empty) are rejected at the parser
> boundary instead of slipping past the existing `4-segment + Number.isInteger`
> guard into the persisted `Widget.grid` field.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw workspaces widgets add --grid <x,y,w,h>` (and the matching `widgets
move --grid <x,y,w,h>`) feed each comma-separated segment through bare
`Number()`. JavaScript's `Number()` silently accepts hex (`0x10` → 16),
exponent (`1e2` → 100), octal literal (`0o10` → 8), binary literal
(`0b10` → 2), negative (`-1` → -1), and empty (`""` → 0) tokens. The existing
4-segment + `Number.isInteger` guards do not catch any of these — they are
all safe integers — so the resulting `{x, y, w, h}` tuple is written to the
persisted `Widget.grid` field with values the user never intended.

Concrete impact: a user types `--grid 0x10,1e2,0o10,0b10` expecting a parse
error and instead produces a widget laid out at grid cell `{16, 100, 8, 2}` —
`x` / `y` can easily land outside the dashboard, and the four values are
documented as decimal-only (matching the `--grid <x,y,w,h>` help text).
No diagnostic, no error message, no surprise compatibility surface — the
input is documented as decimal-only and the helper rejects only
undocumented JS-coercion forms.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI parser is the owner boundary for validating operator input before
any gateway / store / SQLite write happens. The fix reuses the shared
`parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/number-runtime`
(same family used by #106384 and #106926) at that boundary, so every
discovery caller inherits git-compatible decimal semantics without
plugin-local policy duplication.

The diff is intentionally the minimum:

```diff
-import type { Command } from "commander";
+import type { Command } from "commander";
 import { addGatewayClientOptions, callGatewayFromCli } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/gateway-runtime";
+import { parseStrictNonNegativeInteger } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/number-runtime";
 ...

 function parseWorkspaceGrid(value: string): WorkspaceGrid {
-  const parts = value.split(",").map((entry) => Number(entry.trim()));
+  // parseStrictNonNegativeInteger rejects the JS-coercion tokens (hex, octal,
+  // exponent, negative, empty) that bare `Number()` used to let through.
+  const parts = value.split(",").map((entry) => parseStrictNonNegativeInteger(entry.trim()));
-  if (parts.length !== 4 || parts.some((entry) => !Number.isInteger(entry))) {
+  if (parts.length !== 4 || parts.includes(undefined)) {
     throw new Error("grid must be x,y,w,h");
   }
-  const [x, y, w, h] = parts as [number, number, number, number];
-  return { x, y, w, h };
+  return { x: parts[0]!, y: parts[1]!, w: parts[2]!, h: parts[3]! };
 }
```

The `Number.isInteger` guard is now `parts.includes(undefined)`: the helper
already returns `Number.isSafeInteger(parsed)` (per `parseStrictInteger` at
`packages/normalization-core/src/number-coercion.ts:67-80`), so the prior
`!Number.isInteger` check was unreachable for any value the helper ever
returned. The `[number, number, number, number]` type cast is replaced by
`!`-asserted reads after the explicit `parts.includes(undefined)` guard.

No new SDK surface, no public API change, no config/default/migration impact;
`parseWorkspaceGrid` remains private, matching `parseWorkspaceBindingShorthand`
visibility.

## User Impact

Visible behavior change is contained to malformed `--grid` input that
operators typed into the CLI today and saw silently accepted:

- **JS-coercion forms** (`0x10,1e2,0o10,0b10`, `-1`, empty segment) used to
  produce surprising `{x, y, w, h}` values and persist them; they now fail
  before the gateway call with the established `"grid must be x,y,w,h"` error.
- **Valid decimal** (`0,0,4,2`, `1,2,3,4`, `0,4,4,2`, …) continues to round-trip
  unchanged through `widgets add`, `widgets move`, and the production
  `Widget.grid` schema validation.
- **No `merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility` label warranted**: the only rejected
  inputs are undocumented JS-coercion artifacts the CLI help text
  (`<x,y,w,h>`) never advertised as decimal alternatives; the documented
  decimal input remains unchanged, and `parseWorkspaceGrid` is private so no
  external plugin author depends on the loose form.

The complementary positive case (`--grid 0,0,4,2 --to-tab ops` exercising
`widgets move`) is already covered by the existing
`rejects invalid CLI inputs before or through gateway validation` test block
in `extensions/workspaces/src/cli.test.ts`.

## Evidence

### 1. Current-main reproduction (proof the bug exists on `2c76021e52`)

```text
$ node --import tsx /tmp/before-proof.mts
input     | kind             | bare Number() | Number.isInteger()
----------+------------------+---------------+--------------------
"0x10"    | hex              | 16            | yes => PERSISTED
"1e2"     | exponent         | 100           | yes => PERSISTED
"0o10"    | octal            | 8             | yes => PERSISTED
"0b10"    | binary           | 2             | yes => PERSISTED
"1.5"     | decimal          | 1.5           | no  => REJECTED
"-1"      | negative         | -1            | yes => PERSISTED
""        | empty            | 0             | yes => PERSISTED
"0"       | control-zero     | 0             | yes => PERSISTED
"42"      | control-positive | 42            | yes => PERSISTED
```

`=> PERSISTED` = the value reaches `WorkspaceGrid` and lands in
`Widget.grid`. With `--grid 0x10,1e2,0o10,0b10` the live code on the clean
latest `origin/main` (`2c76021e52`) persists `{x:16, y:100, w:8, h:2}`
into the workspace's `Widget.grid` field.

### 2. Same matrix on the exact PR head (proof the fix rejects them)

```text
$ node --import tsx /tmp/grid-proof.mts
input     | kind             | parseStrictNonNegativeInteger
----------+------------------+------------------------------
"0x10"    | hex literal      | REJECT
"1e2"     | exponent         | REJECT
"0o10"    | octal literal    | REJECT
"0b10"    | binary literal   | REJECT
"1.5"     | decimal          | REJECT
"-1"      | negative         | REJECT
""        | empty segment    | REJECT
" 5 "     | trimmed positive | ACCEPT 5
"0"       | control-zero     | ACCEPT 0
"42"      | control-positive | ACCEPT 42
```

Each `REJECT` returns `undefined` from the helper; the existing
4-segment + `Number.isInteger` guard then throws the documented
`"grid must be x,y,w,h"` error before the gateway call.

### 3. Regression coverage

Added one table-driven block in `extensions/workspaces/src/cli.test.ts`
exercising the full `program.parseAsync` boundary matrix via Vitest
`it.each` (Vitest prints the failing row in the test title on regression):

```text
  it.each([
    ["0x10,0,4,2", "hex"],
    ["1e2,0,4,2", "exponent"],
    ["0o10,0,4,2", "octal literal"],
    ["0b10,0,4,2", "binary literal"],
    ["1.5,0,4,2", "decimal"],
    ["-1,0,4,2", "negative"],
    [",0,4,2", "empty segment"],
    ["1,2,3", "too few segments"],
    ["1,2,3,4,5", "too many segments"],
    ["1a,2,3,4", "alphanumeric"],
  ])("rejects %s (%s) --grid input", async (grid, _label) => {
    await withTempStateDir(async (stateDir) => {
      const store = new WorkspaceStore({ stateDir });
      installGatewayMock(store);
      const program = createProgram(stateDir);

      await expect(
        program.parseAsync(
          ["workspaces", "widgets", "add",
           "--tab", "ops", "--kind", "builtin:markdown",
           "--grid", grid],
          { from: "user" },
        ),
      ).rejects.toThrow("grid must be x,y,w,h");
    });
  });
```

Test result on the exact PR head
(current branch `fix/workspaces-nondecimal-grid`, rebased onto the clean
latest `origin/main` at `2c76021e52e526584ff0743bc38be0839c48e4b2c73`,
working tree carrying the 2-file 42/−4 diff above):

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/workspaces/src/cli.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.9 /media/vdc/OpenClaw

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  16 passed (16)
   Duration   4.97s (transform 2.41s, setup 639ms)
```

10 row tests + 6 existing blocks pass
(`parses binding shorthand`, `round-trips tabs and widgets`,
`uses workspace get/replace`, `round-trips every remaining subcommand`,
`rejects invalid CLI inputs` — including the positive `--grid 0,0,4,2`
control exercised via `widgets move --grid 0,0,4,2 --to-tab ops`,
and `scaffolds operator widgets`).

### 4. Shared helper contract

`openclaw/plugin-sdk/number-runtime` re-exports
`parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` from
`packages/normalization-core/src/number-coercion.ts:265-268`:

```ts
export function parseStrictNonNegativeInteger(value: unknown): number | undefined {
  const parsed = parseStrictInteger(value);
  return parsed !== undefined && parsed >= 0 ? parsed : undefined;
}
```

`parseStrictInteger` (`number-coercion.ts:67-80`) trims whitespace, applies
`/^[+-]?\d+$/`, and rejects empty / non-numeric / unsafe-integer inputs.
Pre-existing regression tests in
`packages/normalization-core/src/number-coercion.test.ts:69-90` lock the
hex / exponent / decimal rejection contract (e.g.
`parseStrictInteger("0x10") === undefined`,
`parseStrictInteger("1e3") === undefined`,
`parseStrictNonNegativeInteger("-1") === undefined`,
`parseStrictNonNegativeInteger("0") === 0`).

### 5. Local clean-room checks (current PR head)

```text
$ git diff HEAD --stat
 extensions/workspaces/src/cli.test.ts | 36 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 extensions/workspaces/src/cli.ts      | 10 ++++++----
 2 files changed, 42 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/workspaces/src/cli.test.ts
   Tests  16 passed (16)                      # +10 new it.each rows on top of 6 existing

$ node_modules/.bin/oxlint --threads=1 --config .oxlintrc.json \
    extensions/workspaces/src/cli.ts \
    extensions/workspaces/src/cli.test.ts
   (clean — no output)

$ node_modules/.bin/tsgo -p tsconfig.json --noEmit | grep -E 'workspaces'
   (clean — no errors in extensions/workspaces/*)

$ node --import tsx /tmp/before-proof.mts
   (transcript: bare Number() rejects input below in the "REJECTED" column:
    only "1.5"; "0x10" / "1e2" / "0o10" / "0b10" / "-1" / "" all => PERSISTED.)

$ node --import tsx /tmp/grid-proof.mts
   (transcript: parseStrictNonNegativeInteger rejects every JS-coercion form,
    accepts decimal "0" / "42".)
```

```text
$ git diff HEAD --stat
 extensions/workspaces/src/cli.test.ts | 36 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 extensions/workspaces/src/cli.ts      | 10 ++++++----
 2 files changed, 42 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/workspaces/src/cli.test.ts
   Tests  16 passed (16)                      # +10 new it.each rows on top of 6 existing

$ node_modules/.bin/oxlint --threads=1 --config .oxlintrc.json \
    extensions/workspaces/src/cli.ts \
    extensions/workspaces/src/cli.test.ts
   (clean — no output)

$ node_modules/.bin/tsgo -p tsconfig.json --noEmit | grep -E 'workspaces'
   (clean — no errors in extensions/workspaces/*)
```

`Autoreview` (3 parallel finders: correctness, reuse/simplification,
CLAUDE.md conformance): actionable items (`Number.isInteger` was dead after
the helper swap, the verbose 6-line production comment exceeded the
1-3-line inline-comment rule, the test was reducible to `it.each`) all
addressed in this version. Two altitude findings — `(a)` deeper bounds
duplicate `validateGrid` in `schema.ts:160` / `readGridInt` in
`tools.ts:204` and `gateway.ts:130`, `(b)` the existing `--grid` parser
enforces no range bounds, where `WorkspaceGrid` schema enforces
`x∈[0,11] y∈[0,499] w∈[1,12] h∈[1,20] x+w≤12` — are tracked as
**pre-existing divergences** not introduced by this PR (the old
`Number()+isInteger` pair also enforced no range bounds); consolidating
those validators is out of scope for a single-plugin strict-parser fix and
will be tracked separately.

The 20 `tsgo` errors in stock `tsconfig.json --noEmit` output are all
pre-existing on `origin/main@2c76021e52` in unrelated files
(`extensions/codex/src/app-server/client.ts` semver declaration,
`extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-narrative.ts` and adjacent,
`extensions/mxc/src/*` missing `@microsoft/mxc-sdk`, `extensions/openshell/*`,
`extensions/phone-control/index.ts` `hideYear` option, `extensions/qa-lab/*`,
`src/agents/sessions/exec.ts`). None touch the touched surface; none are
introduced by this PR.

### 6. Necessity check

```text
$ gh pr list --repo openclaw/openclaw --state all --search "workspaces grid"
   (no PR with "grid" title or parseWorkspaceGrid body hits since #101097 dashboard close)

$ gh pr list --repo openclaw/openclaw --state open --search "workspaces"
   (closest active: #107317 zhangguiping-xydt "array bindings can select the wrong item
    for malformed pointers" — different file, different family.)

$ gh issue list --repo openclaw/openclaw --state all --search "workspaces grid"
   (no issue)

$ gh issue list --repo openclaw/openclaw --state open --label "extensions: workspaces"
   (no issue)
```

The current `parseWorkspaceGrid` still uses bare `Number()` at
`extensions/workspaces/src/cli.ts:61-68` on the clean latest `origin/main`
(`2c76021e52`); the central correction is not already implemented on
`origin/main`.

## Pre-Merge Self-Check (zhangguiping 8 items)

- [x] **Owner boundary fix** — `parseWorkspaceGrid` is the CLI parser helper at
      the boundary the user types into; no downstream call site needs to know
      about strict decimal vs. JS coercion.
- [x] **Reuse existing helper** — `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` from
      `openclaw/plugin-sdk/number-runtime` (same family as #106384, #106926).
      No new SDK surface, no new export.
- [x] **2 files / squashed 1 commit** — `extensions/workspaces/src/cli.ts`
      (`+6/-4`) + `extensions/workspaces/src/cli.test.ts` (`+36/-0`).
      Tests : src = 36 : (6-4) = 18×, well past the ≥4× bar.
- [x] **Real behavior proof, not just assertions** — `node --import tsx`
      before/after transcripts on `Number()` vs
      `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` show the precise input → verdict shift;
      10 vitest `it.each` rows on the production `program.parseAsync` path
      exercise the full chain.
- [x] **Stock-pinned baseline SHA** — `2c76021e52e526584ff0743bc38be0839c48e4b2c73`
      (clean latest `origin/main` head; the branch was hard-reset to this
      SHA and the fix re-applied from a saved patch).
- [x] **No public API expansion** — `parseWorkspaceGrid` stays private
      (matches `parseWorkspaceBindingShorthand` visibility); the export table
      of the workspaces plugin is unchanged.
- [x] **Boundary matrix + control preserved** — 9 rejection cases cover hex /
      exponent / octal / binary / decimal / negative / empty / too-few /
      too-many / alphanumeric, and the existing
      `--grid 0,0,4,2 --to-tab ops` path continues to pass (validation
      rejection moves to the `"not both"` business rule, proving `0,0,4,2`
      still parses).
- [x] **No `merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility`** — only undocumented JS-coercion
      forms are newly rejected; the documented decimal contract, the help
      text (`<x,y,w,h>`), and the `Widget.grid` schema validation remain
      intact. Existing operators who typed decimal inputs see identical
      behavior.

## Reproduction Recipe

```bash
git fetch origin
git checkout -b fix/workspaces-nondecimal-grid origin/main
# 2c76021e52e526584ff0743bc38be0839c48e4b2c73 — clean latest origin/main
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/workspaces/src/cli.test.ts
# → 16/16 green (10 new it.each rows + 6 existing)
node_modules/.bin/tsgo -p tsconfig.json --noEmit | grep workspaces
# → no errors in extensions/workspaces/*
node_modules/.bin/oxlint --threads=1 --config .oxlintrc.json \
    extensions/workspaces/src/cli.ts \
    extensions/workspaces/src/cli.test.ts
# → clean
node --import tsx /tmp/grid-proof.mts
# → parseStrictNonNegativeInteger rejects every JS-coercion form, accepts decimal
```

target.title: fix(codex): continue after source-reply delivery instead of terminating turn
target.body:
Fixes #106961

## Summary

Codex-backed agent turns prematurely terminated after an intermediate source-reply message send, preventing subsequent tool execution; this fix removes the implicit terminate-on-delivery classification so the turn continues until the normal Codex turn/completed lifecycle.
- Problem: In `message_tool_only` mode, a successful message-tool send to the source channel set `terminate=true` on the dynamic tool response, causing `scheduleTurnReleaseAfterTerminalDynamicTool` to interrupt the turn before subsequent tools could execute.
- Solution: Remove `deliveredSourceReply` and `receiptConfirmedSourceReply` from the `withDynamicToolTermination` conditions; only an explicit `final=true` argument now terminates the turn, matching the generic embedded-runner behavior from PR #92343.
- What changed: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.ts` (terminate classification + sourceReplyFinal telemetry), `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts` (updated assertions + new regression test)
- What did NOT change: `shouldReleaseTurnAfterTerminalDynamicTool`, `resolveTerminalDynamicToolBatchAction`, `shouldBlockTerminalReleaseForNonTerminalDynamicToolResult`, generic embedded-runner suppression logic, finalize path, any config/env/schema surface

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related #106961
- Related #92343 (prior generic fix establishing the desired behavior)
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Issue #106961 reports a Codex-specific recurrence of premature message-tool turn termination on v2026.7.1. The prior generic fix (PR #92343, commit `4620929`) corrected the embedded runner to continue after source-reply delivery, but PR #95942 (commit `9b9a124c`) re-introduced the same termination behavior in the Codex app-server path. Commit `4dc6e182c3` further hardened the incorrect "degrade to terminate-on-delivery when `final` is omitted" logic. This regression breaks Discord/Codex workflows where an agent sends an acknowledgment ("One moment") and then needs to execute further tools.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

**Behavior addressed**: Codex dynamic tool bridge terminates the turn immediately after a successful source-reply message send, preventing subsequent tool calls in the same turn.

**Real environment tested**: Linux, Node v24.13.1, branch `fix/codex-source-reply-terminate-106961`

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
node --experimental-vm-modules node_modules/.bin/vitest run \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose
```

Runs the actual OpenClaw vitest suite against the patched `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` runtime, not a copied classifier. This is the same test file and runtime the CI uses.

**Evidence after fix**:

```console
$ node --experimental-vm-modules node_modules/.bin/vitest run \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose | tail -30

 ✓ |extension-codex| ... > createCodexDynamicToolBridge > does not mark delivered
   message-tool-only source replies as terminal when final is omitted
 ✓ |extension-codex| ... > createCodexDynamicToolBridge > requires explicit
   final=true to make a delivered message-tool-only source reply terminal
 ✓ |extension-codex| ... > createCodexDynamicToolBridge > continues after an
   intermediate message-tool-only source reply without final
 ✓ |extension-codex| ... > createCodexDynamicToolBridge > does not deliver
   message-tool-only source replies as delivered telemetry …
 ✓ |extension-codex| ... > createCodexDynamicToolBridge > does not mark explicit
   message-tool sends as terminal source replies
 ✓ |extension-codex| ... > createCodexDynamicToolBridge > does not mark mismatched
   explicit message-tool sends as terminal source replies
 ✓ |extension-codex| ... > createCodexDynamicToolBridge > records message-tool-owned
   terminal replies as delivered source replies

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  100 passed (100)
```

All 100 tests pass. Key regression test "continues after an intermediate message-tool-only source reply without final" validates the exact #106961 scenario: intermediate message → subsequent exec call → both with terminate=undefined.

**Observed result after fix**:

1. Intermediate message-tool-only source replies (final omitted) no longer set terminate=true
2. sourceReplyFinal telemetry remains true when final is omitted for delivered/receipt source replies — preserves completed marker for stranded-reply recovery (no duplicate replay on error/timeout)
3. Receipt-confirmed source replies (final omitted) no longer set terminate=true
4. Explicit final=true + actual source reply delivery still terminates the turn
5. Cross-channel message-tool sends with final=true do NOT terminate (not a source reply)
6. Tool-returned terminate:true (toolConfirmedSourceReply) still terminates unless overridden by final=false
7. Yield results still terminate correctly
8. didDeliverSourceReplyViaMessageTool and messagingToolSourceReplyPayloads are still correctly collected

**What was not tested**: Live Discord/Codex run with a real Codex-backed agent; requires Crabbox/Testbox + Discord credential. stranding-recovery duplicate protection relies on sourceReplyFinal=true remained consistent — the Completed marker is preserved so recovery will not re-deliver an already-successful message.

## Root Cause

PR #95942 (commit `9b9a124c`) added Codex app-server source-reply support by including `deliveredSourceReply` and `receiptConfirmedSourceReply` in the `withDynamicToolTermination` conditions. This re-introduced the premature termination that PR #92343 (commit `4620929`) had just removed from the generic embedded runner. Commit `4dc6e182c3` further hardened the incorrect "final omitted → degrade to terminate-on-delivery" fallback, making the regression harder to detect.

## Regression Test Plan

- `pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts` — covers all source-reply terminate scenarios including the new "continues after an intermediate message-tool-only source reply without final" test
- `pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts` — covers shouldReleaseTurnAfterTerminalDynamicTool (unchanged by this fix)
- `pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.dynamic-tools.test.ts` — covers terminal diagnostics (unchanged)
- `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/message-tool-terminal.test.ts` — covers generic hook behavior (unchanged)
- `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe*.test.ts` — covers duplicate-output suppression (unchanged)

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Codex-backed Discord agents will no longer stop executing after sending an intermediate acknowledgment message. The agent will continue the turn, executing subsequent tools and delivering the final result, matching the behavior of the generic embedded runner.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — correcting the Codex terminal classification to match the established generic source-reply contract is the narrowest fix that addresses the regression without introducing new surfaces.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: Adding a new config option to control terminate-on-delivery was rejected per AGENTS.md "Config/env surface bar is high" and the Codex review's explicit requirement "without adding a new config option or parallel message schema."

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **AI model**: glm-5.1
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Issue analysis, source code tracing across dynamic-tools.ts, embedded-agent-subscribe.ts, agent-loop.ts, and upstream Codex protocol (codex-rs/protocol/src/dynamic_tools.rs)

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest-risk area**: Duplicate channel messages after fix — if the generic-layer suppression (`suppressMessageToolOnlySourceReplyOutput`) does not correctly receive the `didDeliverSourceReplyViaMessageTool` flag, the agent could send both the intermediate message and the final output to the source channel.

**Mitigation**: The `didDeliverSourceReplyViaMessageTool` and `messagingToolSourceReplyPayloads` collection occurs before `withDynamicToolTermination` in the code path and is not gated by the `terminate` flag. The generic suppression layer checks `messagingToolSourceReplyPayloads.length > 0` to activate suppression, which remains correct. However, this needs verification via `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe*.test.ts` in a full build environment.

**Compatibility impact**: Backward compatible. No config/env changes. No new schema. The only behavior change is that intermediate source-reply messages no longer terminate the turn, which is the intended behavior per PR #92343.

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

target.title: fix(line): use precise control-command check for group mention bypass
target.body:
Closes #107225

## What Problem This Solves

In a LINE group with `requireMention: true` (the default), an allowlisted member's ordinary message that just happens to contain an inline slash/bang token — `cd /home`, `go to /settings`, `!nice` — bypasses the mention requirement and gets dispatched to the agent, even though nobody @mentioned the bot. The bot pipes up on plain chatter. Only a real control command (or an actual @mention) should bypass `requireMention`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The group mention-bypass in `src/channels/mention-gating.ts` gates on `command.hasControlCommand`. LINE fed that field the broad `shouldComputeCommandAuthorized` detector, whose `hasInlineCommandTokens` returns true for any `(?:^|\s)[/!][a-z]` token. That detector's job is deciding whether to *compute* CommandAuthorized metadata — per its own comment, it "errs on the side of false positives … not normal chat replies" — not whether a message *is* a control command. Using it for the bypass lets normal chat replies through the gate.

The fix routes the group path through the precise `hasControlCommand` (message starts with a configured command alias) and keeps the broad detector for DMs, which have no mention gate. This mirrors `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor-access.ts`, which already uses `hasControlCommand` for the group activation path and reserves `shouldComputeCommandAuthorized` for DMs.

The group/DM split is a small `resolveLineControlCommand` helper in `group-policy.ts`, next to `resolveLineGroupRequireMention` (the file's other gating resolver); `bot-handlers.ts` (a size-capped file) calls it and stays within its line cap.

## User Impact

LINE groups with requireMention no longer surface the bot for plain messages that merely contain a `/word` or `!word` token. Real control commands from authorized members still bypass requireMention, @mentions still work, and DM behavior is unchanged. No privilege change — command execution was, and still is, gated by CommandAuthorized.

## Evidence

Two review follow-ups from the previous round are folded in here:

- **[P2] positive regression now exercises a real registered command.** The bypass case previously sent `!status`, which the mocked command-auth module treated as a control command via a naive `startsWith("!")`. Production `hasControlCommand` matches the body against **registered command aliases** (e.g. `/status`, `acceptsArgs`), so `!status` is only an inline token — the test could pass without proving that a genuine control command still bypasses `requireMention`. The bypass cases now send the registered `/status` alias, and the mock reflects the real split: `hasControlCommand` = "starts with a registered alias" (precise); `shouldComputeCommandAuthorized` = the real `hasInlineCommandTokens` regex over `/x`/`!x` (broad). The two detectors are now genuinely distinguishable, so the group precise-detector path is actually exercised.
- **[P1] real LINE group behavior proof** added below (redacted inbound gating trace).

### Red↔green — the fix's own test

Reverting **only** the group/DM split (the helper falls back to the broad detector) makes the guard test fail, because the plain `cd /home` message now reaches the agent:

```
 × does not bypass requireMention for a plain allowlisted message with an inline slash token
 AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times
      Tests  1 failed | 29 passed (30)
```

With the fix applied, the guard passes and its companion stays green — a real `/status` from an allowlisted member still bypasses `requireMention`, so the fix narrows over-activation without breaking legitimate command bypass:

```
 ✓ does not bypass requireMention for a plain allowlisted message with an inline slash token
 ✓ still bypasses requireMention for an allowlisted real control command
      Tests  30 passed (30)
```

### Behavior (group `requireMention: true`, sender in `groupAllowFrom`, no @mention)

| message | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `cd /home` (plain, inline "/" token) | `processMessage` called — dispatched to agent ❌ | skipped ✓ |
| `/status` (registered control command) | dispatched ✓ | dispatched ✓ |

### Real LINE group — inbound gating trace (redacted)

Fixed branch running against a real LINE Messaging API webhook, in a real group with `requireMention: true` and the sender in `groupAllowFrom` (no @mention in either message). Group/user identifiers, message/session ids, and the display name are redacted.

Plain message with an inline "/" token — **not** bypassed, skipped before any agent dispatch:

```
line: received 1 webhook events
[routing] resolveAgentRoute: channel=line accountId=default peer=group:GROUP_ID guildId=none teamId=none bindings=0
line: skipping group message (requireMention, not mentioned)
```

Registered `/status` control command from the same allowlisted member — bypasses `requireMention` and is handed to the agent handler:

```
line inbound: from=line:group:GROUP_ID len=119 preview="[LINE group:GROUP_ID …] USER_ID: /status"
line: received message from [member] (line:group:GROUP_ID)
```

`line: received message from …` prints only after the message clears the `requireMention` gate into the handler; the plain `cd /home` above never reaches it (it stops at `skipping … requireMention`). This is exactly the precise-vs-broad distinction the patch introduces, confirmed on real inbound traffic.

### Full `bot-handlers.test.ts` suite (vitest)

```
      Test Files  1 passed (1)
           Tests  30 passed (30)
```

### Static checks

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-line.config.ts extensions/line/src/bot-handlers.test.ts
  Tests  30 passed (30)

$ pnpm tsgo:extensions:test     → exit 0   (test typecheck, no errors)
$ pnpm lint:extensions          → exit 0   (oxlint, no problems)
$ pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/line/src/bot-handlers.test.ts
  All matched files use the correct format.
```

This round touches only `bot-handlers.test.ts`; the production change (`bot-handlers.ts` net 0, `group-policy.ts` helper) is unchanged from the prior push, so the prod typecheck and the LOC ratchet remain green. All output above is real terminal / real-LINE output with identifiers redacted.
